title: Answering guidance for the questions a person has to answer (one pillar per file)
description: A flat map keyed by control id, deliberately not re-nested by principle: the catalogue owns that structure, and a second copy of it here would be a second thing to keep in step. Guidance lives outside config/controls because those files are generated by seed-catalogue.mjs and a re-seed would clobber authored prose.

pillar.description: The pillar id this file covers, which must match the file name and the catalogue's own id.

entries.description: Keyed by control id. Every key must exist in the catalogue; check-guidance refuses an orphan, which is how a rename is caught the day it happens.

status.description: A draft is a scaffold with nothing written yet and the app says so rather than showing half an answer. An authored entry must satisfy every length rule below, which is what stops an entry shipping as 'TBD'.

last_reviewed.description: When a person last read this against the current framework. Required once authored, because this content has to survive years of revisions and an unread entry is worse than an absent one.

owner_role.description: Who typically holds the answer — 'Platform administrator', 'Data engineering lead'. Attestations already carry an owner; this is who to ask before one exists.

means.description: What the practice means, in plain terms. No marketing, no restating the title.

matters.description: Why it matters, stated as the risk of not doing it. A consequence, not a virtue.

good.description: What good looks like, as concrete signals. This is the answer rubric: a reader compares their estate against these and the comparison decides the answer.

examples.description: Three worked examples so a customer can place themselves honestly rather than aspirationally. Partial is the one that does the work: without it, everyone is strong.

verify.description: Where to look, so an answer is evidence-backed rather than remembered.

pitfalls.description: The ways this is commonly got wrong, including the ways that look right.

partial_when.description: When 'partially' is the honest answer. Absent this, a reader with a half-done practice picks whichever whole answer flatters them.

not_applicable_when.description: When the requirement genuinely does not apply. Omitted where it always applies, which is most of them — and omitting it is a statement rather than an oversight, so check-guidance does not require it.

references.description: Beyond the WAF anchor the control already carries. Nothing checks that these still resolve: the scheduled docs-drift job compares catalogue anchors against the harvested framework and does not fetch arbitrary URLs, so a moved page here is found by a reader. Whoever sets last_reviewed is the check.

allOf.comment: An authored entry carries the fields the panel needs. Enforced here rather than only in check-guidance so a hand edit is caught by the same rule as a generated one.

advice.description: What to do about the requirement, as against how to answer a question about it. Every field is required because the six are one argument: a starting position with no trade-offs beside it is a recommendation with its cost hidden, and a path with no review trigger is a project rather than a practice. Optional as a block and complete within it — the same shape as `examples`, and for the same reason, which is that a half-written dimension renders as advice and reads as authored.

start_from.description: The safe, supportable default for a customer with no established policy. A position somebody could adopt on Monday, not a principle: 'unless you have a reason, do X' rather than 'consider your requirements'.

depends_on.description: The conditions that strengthen, relax or change that default, each naming what it changes it to. Two at least, because a recommendation with one exception is a recommendation whose author only thought of one.

path.description: The staged route from the observed state to a baseline and then to the target, in order. At least two stages: a single step is a target, and the reason this field exists is that a customer far from the target needs somewhere to stand in between.

costs.description: What following the path costs — money, complexity, availability, latency, or somebody's week. Required rather than optional: advice with no stated cost is advice nobody has weighed, and a reader who finds the cost themselves afterwards stops trusting the rest.

retain.description: The artefact that will prove this at the next review — an export, a policy document, a dashboard, a ticket. Named specifically enough to go and find, because 'evidence of the process' is what a reader writes down when nobody said what to keep.

revisit.description: The event or cadence that should reopen the decision. An event where one exists — a migration, a new region, a doubling of the estate — because a date alone gets deferred and an event arrives whether or not anybody is watching for it.

check.comment: `expect` joined `how` and `where` as required in 100a. It was optional while its own description below said a location with no expectation is half a check, and all 191 steps in the corpus carried one — so the rule failed nothing on the day it landed and closes the door behind the entries already written, which is the shape of the citation rule in check-guidance.mjs. Measured before adopting: config/guidance is the only producer of these, scaffolded entries carry no verify block at all, and scripts/recordings/guidance-standard.json holds the reading.

how.description: Which kind of check this is, so the panel can group them and a reader can skip the ones they cannot run.

where.description: The path, the statement or the endpoint. Specific enough to follow without knowing the product. The cap was 400 until a correct statement needed more: `system.lakeflow.job_run_timeline` records a row per period of a run rather than per run, so any duration has to aggregate to the run in a CTE before averaging, and the shorter version of that query was only shorter because its aliases said nothing. A budget is worth keeping to stop a fifty-line query being pasted in; it is not worth naming a column `secs` for.

expect.description: What the reader should see if the practice is in place. A location with no expectation is half a check.

caveat.description: What this check cannot tell you, where a clean result would otherwise be read as a good one. Its own field rather than a longer `expect` because the two are different claims: a review of the first authored pillars found checks whose most important property was the population they silently exclude — `system.query.history` holds nothing from classic compute, `system.information_schema` cannot see the legacy metastore — and an expectation ending in a caveat is an expectation a reader stops before the end of.
